meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-25 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Evan Chen, Sofia Alvarez (Redwood); Alex Turner, Maya Singh, Jordan Lee (Peregrine Retail)
summary: Redwood walked Peregrine through Eval / Quality Monitoring capabilities in Console and Optimize. Covered prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons, and API integration. Discussed security, metrics that matter (RAG hallucinations, F1 for extraction tasks, classification accuracy), and pilot scope. Agreed to exchange prompt sets and run a short pilot benchmark. Open questions: data residency for logs, KMS integration, and cost per eval metric at scale.
transcript:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on this account. I'll do quick intros - Sofia's our solutions engineer, she'll run the demo.
[00:12] Alex (Peregrine): Hi all, Alex here, head of ML at Peregrine. Maya and Jordan with me.
[00:18] Maya (Peregrine): Hi.
[00:20] Sofia (Redwood): Great, quick agenda - we want to show Eval / Quality Monitoring in the Console, how prompt sets map to regression alerts, and how you can do A/B comparisons and tie this into Optimize recommendations.
[00:33] Jordan (Peregrine): Sounds good, main goals: we want to detect when a model degrades after a deploy and to compare model variants for the same prompts, plus keep an eye on hallucinations for our product descriptions use-case.
[00:45] Sofia: Perfect, that's exactly what these features are built for. I'll share my screen - bear with auto-share.
[01:10] [screen share starts] Sofia: Alright, Console -> Evaluate. On the left you can see prompt bundles, we typically create a "prompt set" per use-case - e.g., product-summary, price-extraction, chat-assist. You can import via CSV or API.
[01:38] Alex: Is the import expecting any schema? We have a few fields like context, expected label, acceptability threshold.
[01:45] Sofia: Yeah you can attach expected outputs and one or more metrics; the template includes text_input, expected_output, metric_type (e.g., BLEU, F1, exact match), and tags. We'll share the template.
[02:10] Maya: And how do you run an A/B? We have two models - a smaller quantized variant and a newer 70B. Cost's a concern.
[02:20] Sofia: You can create an A/B job - pick the prompt set and the two model endpoints. Console runs both across the set and reports per-example differences, aggregate metrics, and p-value for stat significance. Also cost-per-query breakdown appears so you can balance accuracy vs cost.
[02:45] Jordan: Nice. Does it stream results or is it batch?
[02:50] Sofia: Typically batch, but we show streaming previews for a sample subset. Full runs are queued and you get dashboards with alert thresholds.
[03:05] Alex: For regression alerts, what triggers - absolute metric drop vs relative?
[03:12] Sofia: You can define triggers as absolute (e.g., F1 drops below 0.85) or relative (e.g., drop >5% vs baseline). We also support rolling baselines, and you can set sensitivity and mute windows.
[03:28] Evan: A lot of customers like to hook alerts to PagerDuty or Slack. We have webhooks and built-in integrations.
[03:35] Alex: Okay, good. Security - do logs of prompts and outputs leave our VPC in Dedicated or Private deployments?
[03:44] Evan: For Redwood Private and Dedicated, logs can be kept within your VPC; we support customer-managed KMS for encryption and can disable payload retention if needed. For hosted, we have options but standard retention is minimal - we'll follow up with the SOC2 and retention policy doc.
[04:02] Maya: KMS is important, plus audit logs for who ran which eval.
[04:08] Sofia: Yep audit trail is in the Console and exportable.
[04:12] [05:00] Sofia: Now I'll run a demo job - here's a product-description prompt set we prepared; note that some transcriptions earlier were off, so ignore model names spelled wrong.
[05:20] [05:20] Sofia: Running an A/B between redwood-70b and redwood-8q. You can see per-example diff heatmap - this is helpful to spot classes where one model hallucinates.
[05:40] Alex: Can we group by tag? Like only electronics or only clearance items?
[05:45] Sofia: Yes, tags filter the prompt set and you can slice and dice by metadata - even by customer segment.
[06:05] Evan: Also note the Optimize tab recommends quantization and batching settings per model to reach a target latency or cost.
[06:18] Maya: On the regression alert, is there support for human review workflows? e.g., flagging failing examples to labelers?
[06:25] Sofia: Absolutely - failing examples can be exported to a labeling queue or to your annotation tool via webhook. We also provide sampling strategies for triage.
[06:40] Jordan: What metrics should we track for hallucinations? Precision? F1? Is there a hallucination-specific heuristic?
[06:49] Sofia: It depends - for extraction tasks F1/exact match works. For generative descriptions, we recommend a combination: entailment checks, keyword overlap, and human-judgment scores. We have a built-in hallucination detector model you can plug in to flag risky outputs.
[07:10] Alex: That sounds useful. How do we calibrate thresholds? We don't want too many false positives.
[07:18] Sofia: Start with a smaller seed set, run A/B, and tune thresholds to balance precision/recall. We also provide ROC curves and confusion matrices for binary metrics.
[07:36] Evan: Quick interjection - some customers prefer to run evaluation jobs in their own infra to avoid sending payloads. We support running the eval runner in Private.
[07:46] Alex: That's probably where we'll land if pilot goes well.
[08:00] [08:00] Sofia: I'll show the alert config - alert on relative drop >5% and F1 < 0.88 will trigger a page and create a ticket. You can set a runbook link and assign team.
[08:20] Maya: Can alerts be suppressed during retrain windows?
[08:24] Sofia: Yes you can set maintenance windows or mute for X hours post-deploy.
[08:32] Jordan: How do we hook this into our canary rollouts? We want automatic rollback if a metric drops severely.
[08:40] Sofia: We offer integration with rollout policies - if the A/B or canary shows critical degradation, you can auto-fallback to a previous pinned version. That's configurable per-route.
[08:55] Alex: Great. On the API side, how easy is it to programmatically create prompt sets and run evals?
[09:02] Sofia: We have REST endpoints and SDKs. Example flows: push CSV, kick eval job, poll for results or subscribe to webhooks. We'll share a Postman collection and an SDK snippet.
[09:18] Evan: We'll attach a sample script you can run in a sandbox.
[09:22] Alex: Any limitations on size of prompt sets? We might have 50k examples for a large sweep.
[09:30] Sofia: For hosted, larger runs are queued but supported; Dedicated/Private can run faster depending on reserved capacity. We can advise on batching and sharding. For very large corpuses we recommend breaking into staged runs.
[09:50] Maya: Cost - curious how you show cost per metric.
[09:55] Sofia: In the A/B run summary we show token-level cost per-model and compute cost per-example. Optimize will recommend a cheaper variant if quality delta is marginal.
[10:08] Jordan: So if 8q gives 95% of quality at 30% of cost, Optimize will suggest that?
[10:14] Sofia: Yup, and you can lock a policy to prefer cost-savings unless quality drops more than X.
[10:22] Alex: About model variants, can we include third-party models like OpenAI or self-hosted endpoints?
[10:28] Sofia: Yes, you can compare across Redwood-hosted models, dedicated endpoints, and external endpoints (we proxy metrics; for external you need to provide latency/cost metadata).
[10:40] Jordan: We heard some vendors do a poor job aligning metrics with business KPIs. How do you link evals to product metrics?
[10:48] Sofia: You can attach tags and mapping rules; for example map prompt set results to an NPS delta or cart conversion metric. We also support sending aggregated evaluation events to your analytics pipeline.
[11:05] [11:05] Alex: Can you demo a regression alert flow?
[11:12] Sofia: Sure - here's a triggered alert from a previous run. Clicking expands per-example context, the model output, expected output, and historical trend. You can open the triage view and assign to a reviewer.
[11:32] Maya: The transcript shows some weird tokenization in one example - is that from the speech-to-text?
[11:38] Sofia: Oh yeah the demo prompt had a punctuation edge case, you'll see some imperfect matches in transcripts, not the eval.
[11:46] Jordan: How long does it take to get results for a 5k prompt set?
[11:50] Sofia: On Hosted maybe a few hours depending on queue; with Dedicated it'll finish in under an hour with reserved GPU throughput.
[12:02] Alex: For our pilot we'll likely do 5k examples across three use-cases.
[12:08] Sofia: That's a great size to start. We'll show a baseline and then run A/B to choose a candidate for production.
[12:20] Evan: Quick pause - any legal or procurement blockers we should know of?
[12:26] Alex: Procurement needs SOC2 and data processing addendum; security wants KMS and retention controls.
[12:30] Evan: We'll send SOC2 report and DPA template. Note on Dedicated/Private we can accommodate KMS.
[12:37] Maya: Does Redwood support SSO with our IdP?
[12:40] Sofia: Yes SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning.
[12:44] [13:00] Sofia: Now switching to Optimize - here's the recommendation engine. It looks at your workload distribution and suggests quantization profiles, batching windows, and cache TTLs to hit target p50 latency or cost threshold.
[13:20] Alex: Any automated A/B of quantization profiles? We saw in the docs some auto-validate pipeline.
[13:26] Sofia: There is an auto-validation step - run a small eval to ensure quality doesn't drop beyond a chosen delta after quantization. If it passes, the profile can be promoted.
[13:36] Jordan: For caching - prefix cache might help product description completions, but we worry about staleness.
[13:42] Sofia: You can set TTLs and cache invalidation hooks from your data pipeline. Optimize will also simulate cache hit rates based on historical prompt distribution.
[13:55] Alex: Great. On telemetry, can we get token-level cost tied to route/user so we can chargebacks internally?
[14:02] Evan: Yes, Console has per-route breakdown and you can tag requests with tenant IDs for internal chargeback.
[14:10] Maya: Ok that's necessary.
[14:14] [15:00] Jordan: A hypothetical - if an eval shows a 7% drop in F1 after a deploy, what is typical flow?
[15:08] Sofia: Alert -> triage -> if severity high, auto-roll back or route traffic to previous version -> create ticket and export failing examples for labeling -> re-train or tune.
[15:20] Alex: And SLOs - can we set SLOs that are evaluated automatically?
[15:25] Sofia: Yes SLOs are first-class. You can set targets per-route and get history and burn-rate alerts.
[15:34] Evan: We should discuss scope for pilot: propose 3 prompt sets (~5k each), run baseline vs two candidate models, configure regression alerts with relative >5% sensitivity, and create a weekly dashboard.
[15:50] Alex: Sounds good, timeline?
[15:53] Evan: If you can get prompt sets in by April 1, we can run the benchmark the week of April 6 and have results the same week.
[16:00] Maya: That works. Procurement timeline might take a couple weeks but we can run the pilot on a trial account or Dedicated eval credits?
[16:10] Evan: We can provision a trial Dedicated slot for the pilot; I'll work with sales ops.
[16:18] Jordan: Any limitations on PII in prompts? Our product descriptions occasionally include vendor-provided contact info.
[16:25] Sofia: You can redact or use tokenization. For Private deployments you can keep PII in VPC; for hosted we recommend hashed or redacted prompts if retention is a concern.
[16:38] Alex: Are there any gotchas with embeddings-based similarity evals?
[16:44] Sofia: Embedding drift can affect thresholds; we recommend periodically re-embedding the baseline and using cosine distribution checks. We also surface embedding QC metrics in the Console.
[16:58] Evan: Quick note - competitors like OpenAI don't provide the same unified eval + optimize + routing tooling, so customers often stitch together many tools.
[17:08] Maya: Right.
[17:10] Jordan: Anything else from your side?
[17:12] Alex: No, I think we covered the main points.
[17:15] Sofia: Ok I'm going to share the eval bundle link in the chat, plus the prompt set template.
[17:22] Evan: I'll follow up with pricing, SOW, and security docs.
[17:26] [crosstalk] Maya: Quick question on retention periods again-
[17:30] Evan: We'll include options in the DPA.
[17:35] Jordan: Great.
[17:40] Sofia: Next steps in chat - we'll recap.
[17:45] Alex: Thanks folks, this was helpful.
[17:48] Evan: Thanks everyone.
[17:50] [call ends]
notes: Demo covered A/B, regression alerts, prompt set templates, Optimize recommendations, and Private deployment options for PII/KMS. Peregrine to send prompt sets; Redwood to provide SOC2 and SOW. Potential Dedicated trial for pilot.
